## Purpose and executable surface
Komari is a self-hosted Go server-monitoring and remote-control backend. `main.go` launches the Cobra CLI rooted at `cmd/root.go`; the server command in `cmd/server.go` initializes the application. It serves embedded frontend assets, HTTP/WebSocket/JSON-RPC APIs, accepts reports from lightweight agents, persists monitoring history, and provides terminal/file-control capabilities.

## Application bootstrap and lifecycle
`internal/server/app.go` is the composition root for runtime services; `internal/server/bootstrap.go` handles startup sequencing, while `internal/server/runtime.go` and `internal/server/reload.go` manage running state and configuration reload. Configuration is loaded from `internal/config/config.go` and `internal/config/settings.go`. Restart behavior is isolated in `internal/lifecycle/restart.go`.

## HTTP, RPC, and access boundary
The Gin-facing router in `web/router/router.go` exposes public, authenticated, admin, client, install, migration, recovery, upload, and WebSocket surfaces. JSON-RPC dispatch and registration live in `web/rpc/jsonrpc/dispatch.go`, `web/rpc/jsonrpc/register.go`, and `web/rpc/jsonrpc/transport.go`; authorization semantics are centralized by `pkg/rpc/permission.go`, `pkg/rpc/principal.go`, and `pkg/rpc/registry.go`. CORS/origin policy is a separate security boundary in `web/security/cors.go` and `web/security/origin.go`.

## Agent connectivity and live control
Agents connect through `web/agent/connections.go`; protocol-v2 events are processed in `web/agent/v2_events.go`. Client endpoints accept discovery, presence, basic metadata, and metric reports, notably `web/api/client/report_v2.go` and `web/api/client/ingest.go`. WebSocket transport enables live UI updates and control. Terminal establishment/forwarding is handled under `web/api/terminal/`, while agent-mediated file transfer and stream relay are in `web/filemanager/transfer.go` and `web/filemanager/stream_relay.go`.

## Persistence and metric pipeline
SQLite-oriented database initialization and maintenance are in `database/dbcore/dbcore.go` and `database/dbcore/maintenance.go`; domain repositories cover accounts, clients, tasks, notifications, audit logs, clipboard, and records. Historical metrics are owned by `internal/metricstore/store.go`, with report batching/mapping in `internal/metricstore/report_batcher.go` and `internal/metricstore/report_mapping.go`. The reusable metric engine in `pkg/metric/store.go` implements raw points, aggregation, rollups, retention/restructuring, and SQL dialect support, including PostgreSQL integration.

## Scheduling, migrations, and operational maintenance
Periodic work is coordinated by `internal/scheduler/scheduler.go`, alongside persisted ping/task logic in `database/tasks/ping.go` and `database/tasks/tasks.go`. Startup/evolution migrations are in `internal/migrations/migrations.go` and legacy-monitoring migration paths in `internal/migrations/legacy_monitoring.go`. Metric compaction, deletion, recovery, and maintenance are explicit stages under `internal/metricstore/`.

## Extensibility and outbound integrations
The plugin subsystem installs, versions, runs, and communicates with plugins through `internal/plugin/plugin.go`, `internal/plugin/install.go`, `internal/plugin/server.go`, and `internal/plugin/rpc.go`. Its JavaScript execution environment is implemented in Go under `pkg/jsruntime/runtime.go` and `pkg/jsruntime/node_runtime.go`, with Node-like HTTP, filesystem, process, and event APIs. Themes/plugins can be managed and downloaded through admin APIs. Notifications use persisted sender settings plus adapters in `utils/messageSender/`, supporting email, Telegram, webhooks, Bark, ServerChan, and JavaScript senders; OAuth providers are implemented under `web/oauth/`.

## Deployment and external dependencies
The primary runtime is a Go binary, containerized by `Dockerfile`; release/build automation includes Docker publication workflows. The embedded frontend is served through `web/public/embedded.go`. Core infrastructure is the local database (with metric SQL abstractions that also support PostgreSQL); external interactions include managed agents, OAuth identity providers, notification endpoints, plugin/theme markets, GeoIP providers, and HTTP-accessible update/download sources.
